meaning: A secret number, often four digits, that you type to prove it is you. Phones, bank cards, and apps use it.
clues: It helps prove who you are.
It is made of numbers only.
You choose it yourself, and you type it in to open a phone or use a bank card.
It is short, and you should never share it or let anyone watch you type it.
It has three letters. The first, P, stands for personal.
assumes: A security question is answered in words
A one-time code is sent to you and works once

decoys.meaning: A personal question you pick when you set up an account, like your first pet's name. You answer it later to prove who you are.
A short code sent to you for one sign-in only. It stops working after a few minutes.
A way to open a phone by looking at it. The phone checks that your face matches the one it saved.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, the only number I knew by heart was my locker combination.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: A PIN works the same way. Skip 1234 and birthdays, and never tell it to a caller, even one who says they are from your bank.

sources.name: FDIC, Banking at the Speed of Technology
